text.p: A few hints that the worst of the recent supply tightness that has been driving LME copper prices higher was over prompted a late afternoon sell-off.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index rose 0.19 points to 241.44 points.

On the LME, three months delivery copper last traded at $2,437 a tonne, down $74 from Monday's close, after touching a five-week low of $2,430. Traders said the failure of the market to convincingly pierce $2,600 earlier in the month, a narrowing in the spread, a few small warehouse stock increases and the approaching summer slow-down all combined to take the heat out of the buy side.
Among other metals copper's sell-off caused a downward adjustment in zinc and aluminium.
Profittaking hit zinc which gave up the $1,400 level in the late afternoon to end at $1,397, down $11.5 from Monday.

But aluminium continued to disappoint its supporters, failing to test $1,590 resistance despite the continuing fall in LME warehouse stocks. It succumbed to liquidation orders late in the day to finally trade at $1,577 a tonne, down $13.
Nickel drifted lower on the prospect of the Inco talks resuming and three months delivery ended the afternoon kerb trading at $7,170, down $40 from Monday.
Lead ended just below $620, down around $4, tin at $5,580, down $40, and alloy at $1,467, unchanged.

Gold ender lower in line with other precious metals traded on NYMEX and COMEX. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted at US$337.50/00, after gold fixed in London on Tuesday afternoon at US$338.35 an ounce.

IPE Brent futures closed lower on Tuesday after news that Iraq is to start exporting oil from the second tranche of its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations in the next seven to 10 days, traders said. August Brent settled 11 cents down at $17.87 a barrel having tumbled as low as $17.73 on the Iraqi oil export news. July Gas oil closed unchanged at $160.25 a tonne.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on a slowdown in harvesting of hard red winter wheat and on oversold signals, traders said. Cash grain dealers said rain halted the harvest early Tuesday in portions of southern Kansas, northern Texas and parts of Oklahoma. CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed 1-1/2 to 3-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with July up 2-3/4 at $3.32-1/2 a bushel. September was up two cents at $3.39.
